title: Practical Revolutionary Networking
author: MTCSTW
text: Why it matters : As leftists, we need to be actively forging bonds with people from all walks of life, but especially within and between leftist circles. Let’s say we get our way, and the Imperial Core is dismantled and replaced with a leftist governing body of some sort. That’s not likely to be a clean transition, and collective, coordinated action will be necessary to deflect reactionary counter-revolutionaries and support at-risk community members mid-transition. First and foremost, leftist organizing should be centered on genuine compassion and operationalized empathy— even fired-up black bloc counter-protesters are motivated primarily by compassion for vulnerable people and engaging in community defense against fascist harassment and assault as an operationalized form of empathy. Of equal import is sincerity and genuine engagement amongst peers in different organizations . Developing connections between affinity groups and organizations to coordinate responses and developing message discipline for shared goals would benefit the Left greatly. That will require us to be willing to (respectfully and with permission, of course) enter spaces we’re not familiar with, commiserate with group members sincerely and without pretense. Be real. Make some friends while you’re at it. Don’t just robotically collect new comrades’ contact info. One durable, mutually supportive connection is worth multiple superficial or tenuous connections. title: Capitalism Broke Us. Now It's Charging Us To Get "Fixed"
author: MTCSTW
text: Why it Matters: The wellness/alternative medicine/supplement industries are barely regulated and often have safety practices that aren’t very safe but are very profitable. Yet again it’s profit motive vs the health of our society. ICYMI: Moreno Neurospicy News is now on Substack ! Check out my independent work at SLSC on Substack ! Share The Propaganda Factory I need to tell you something that might ruin your morning kale and quinoa smoothie. That $6.3 trillion wellness industry selling you solutions to your stress, burnout, and exhaustion? It’s profiting from problems it helped create. Like an arsonist with a very successful fire extinguisher business. I’m watching companies install massage chairs in offices where they won’t install living wages. I’m seeing corporations push meditation apps while engineering 60-hour work weeks designedengineered to break you. And I’m done pretending the irony isn’t palpable. The Math Doesn’t Add Up The wellness industry grew from $4.6 trillion in 2020 to $6.3 trillion by 2023. That’s roughly four times larger than the entire pharmaceutical industry. Meanwhile, burnout keeps getting worse. Funny how that works. By 2026, global corporate spending on wellness programs will top $94.6 billion. Nearly 85% of large U.S. employers already offer workplace wellness programs—because nothing says “we care” like mandatory resilience training. And yet the mental health crisis these programs claim to solve continues to escalate. Almost like they were never

text: It's spring and organizing season is here again! The 2025-2026 winter saw ICE/CBP brutality and the murder of two protesters in broad daylight, a sovereign leader deposed and held in a foreign prison, and an illegal war against a sovereign nation. It's on us to resist the rising tide of fascism , and there's no better time like the present to start — get out your head-to-toe black outfits, red flags, and head to the barricades! Okay, it’s not gonna be that flashy, at least not all the time. But it is necessary. Dedicated people with focus and drive are needed more than ever these days. In order to build the parallel structures we’ll need if (read: when) America finally loses steam and is relegated to former empire status, like Great Britain or the Ottomans. One day we too might have a funny decorative stool named for, perhaps, our crumbling infrastructure. Just Do Something! It's less important that you do any particular thing and more that something gets done. There's a world of problems to tackle and addressing the ones that you know best and have access to will get the most “bang for your buck” when getting started. Most important is that you develop the habits of an organizer and adopt the mindset necessary for movement-building. Your first cause will likely not be your last. Many small projects snowball into bigger ones or merge with complimentary causes to create a larger, more formidable force that's harder for those in power to reckon with. You never know where a small, well-executed idea will end up with enough time and effort dedicated to it. Cycling Periods of Rest and Avoiding Burnout Like any other skill, organizing requires a fair amount of work, a strong knowledge base, and a level of dedication not everyone can maintain long enough to be effective. Unlike individual pursuits, organizing is a team effort, requiring coordination and communication in ways that other ways of making an impact on society do not. Once you’ve been working with people for a while, you’ll begin to notice when they are the most active and what time of year they really need to be able to focus on themselves. Until such time though, varying workloads and making sure even the most trying of try-hards (no shade; I was usually active in at least four or five working groups at a time) don’t have to shoulder the whole load. With that said, any organization is going to need particularly active people. It’s very much a learn by doing sort of thing, though I’d suggest reading the organizer’s classic Rules for Radicals , which any alternative bookstore worth their salt should carry. title: Sociologist In Search of Economist to Co-Author New Theory & Praxis
author: MTCSTW
text: Hey so — things have gotten pretty bad around here, huh? Quality of life is down. Options are shrinking. The language we’ve been taught to explain this… “free markets,” “efficiency,” “scarcity,” has always been a self-protecting system of logic and reason SO, economists who know the math is not mathing; WHERE ARE YOU?! The People are calling on all economists to realign with the working class & help us hold the billionaires accountable for their crimes against society & humanity at large. I’m a sociologist focused on the intersection of poverty, mental/physical health, & parenting through multigenerational traumas. I am looking to collaborate with a fellow academic / trained economist who is willing to help me rewrite the defaults. I’m not trying to critique. I want to build something new . I’m interested in developing: a framework that actually reflects how people live and function (not how models assume they do/should) language that can easily translate across academic, public, and advocacy spaces something practical & tangible — I’m talking policy, tools, strategy If you’ve been feeling the gap between what economics says and what people experience , we should probably connect. I’ll be here. Writing. Swirling. Waiting for you. Message Sarah A. Russell Thanks for reading my scream into the void. Share this post to help me find my soulmate! title: After The Fall: Getting To The Future We Deserve
author: MTCSTW
text: The Problem At Hand It’s not hard to tell America is in the shitter right now. Relative to its former position in the world, the empire is beginning to noticeably crumble. Problems persist throughout the country, with the resulting pain felt first and most acutely by people of color, the impoverished, the LGBTQ+ community, the disabled, and other marginalized people. The nation’s infrastructure is crumbling beneath our feet. Our schools are in the proverbial toilet. Our food is all overprocessed and undernutritious, packaged for mass consumption rather than a people’s nourishment. Even our water is being poisoned, and even more so with each new data center brought online. These problems affect us all to some degree, and the damage is becoming impossible to ignore, yet resistance to change is met on multiple fronts. Lobbyists and Monied Interests The American system of governance is choked with lobbyists and private corporation interests who are deep in the pockets of both Democrats and Republicans in office. Things have been corrupt since the initial colonization of the US, and private property was always valued as more important a right even than human rights (just look at how many slave owners signed onto the Declaration of independence). Today, our rights and dignity are sacrificed before the altar of private interest via the destruction and exploitation of natural resources and the environment. Every server farm built to mine crypto is another golden calf at the altar of

title: After The Fall: Getting To The Future We Deserve
author: MTCSTW
text: ficed before the altar of private interest via the destruction and exploitation of natural resources and the environment. Every server farm built to mine crypto is another golden calf at the altar of capitalism. Every insider trade makes the foul, acrid smoke of the incense. Every presidential scam (at the expense of his own base) lays bare the dynamic- people sacrificed for profit. A Population Traumatized And what happens when the Trumpistas are scammed in this way? They come crawling back to huck a couple more nickels at the Golden Calf. He moos proudly, and they receive their dopamine-hit-blessing and “own the libs ” by pissing away their cash on snake oil and Trumpcoin. They are marks, little more than the targets of exploitation, and yet we are held hostage in their subjugation with them because a few too many people with too-short memories were fooled into backing a charlatan. On the other side of the coin are the Battered Blues, neglected year after year in service of donors. Neither party provides the material gains they promise or imply promises of, and the malaise only continues to deepen. Available Solutions We have before us a few solutions to this problem. Approaches to reconciling irreconcilable differences rarely are fruitful, so a so-called National Divorce has been called for by some on both the left and the right. The Enlightened Centrist will tell you to pipe down and suck it up, and keep taking the abuse and neglect. I would say, why divorce the two corru

title: After The Fall: Getting To The Future We Deserve
author: MTCSTW
text: een called for by some on both the left and the right. The Enlightened Centrist will tell you to pipe down and suck it up, and keep taking the abuse and neglect. I would say, why divorce the two corrupted parents and leave the children- their constituents- in the hands of these unfit stewards any longer. It is time to emancipate these minors and allow them agency over their own selves. But by what means should this emancipation come about? Reform Some argue that reform by borderline pacifistic means is the only way forward. Fears of backlash, pendulum swings, and other forms of revolt against the new order often make change by reform slow and incremental and – most troublingly of all – inadequate. Others suggest that pushing the envelope with a militant wing is more effective, and we see examples of this throughout history. From the Civil Rights Movement of 20th century America to the British suffragette movement, we see how the militancy of a disciplined group of hardliners ultimately made reform possible by shifting the Overton Window. Still, we are left insufficient results , though the gains made are undeniably meaningful in the context of the gradual change to which we must often acquiesce (for we are often afforded no more choices on the matter). Revolution The other side of the “coin” that is social change, revolution, also comes in a sort of spectrum of forms, ranging from political revolutionary talk – i.e. seizing the means of production and governance from the ruli

title: After The Fall: Getting To The Future We Deserve
author: MTCSTW
text: f the “coin” that is social change, revolution, also comes in a sort of spectrum of forms, ranging from political revolutionary talk – i.e. seizing the means of production and governance from the ruling class via mass movement politics – to full-blown violent overthrow. Personally, I would see the latter as a means of last resort, only to be embarked upon once all other avenues have been exhausted. The risk of counterrevolution and government retaliation/crackdown is very real under these circumstances, and such tactics put at risk a great number of vulnerable people should they be found to be sympathetic. This can create rifts in the revolution that become extremely problematic if allowed to bleed without any sort of bandaging. Subscribe Share “Popular Militancy” I believe that a space between the two poles of revolution exists that may be worth exploring. By preserving the revolutionary spirit, but employing the militant-non-militant wings approach of many reform movements, a synthesis may be found with enough force and staying power that real change might be achieved. On one hand, a non-violent, political wing doing the organizing and electoral maneuvering – without compromising an inch with fascists and liberals – to seize power, exercise it, and return governance to popular control. On the other, the militant, in-the-streets wing to handle both proactive, aggressive street action and the nitty-gritty, unpleasant counterattacks of capital; a sword and shield against the c

title: After The Fall: Getting To The Future We Deserve
author: MTCSTW
text: control. On the other, the militant, in-the-streets wing to handle both proactive, aggressive street action and the nitty-gritty, unpleasant counterattacks of capital; a sword and shield against the cops, owners, and agitators who would see capital remain in the hands of the powerful whose boots they lick. Once communities are rebuilt in a saner, more egalitarian way such that they can engage in participatory self-governance earnestly and without barrier to entry for any person, the state should be dissolved and the communities, having fully developed, be returned to communal stewardship. Similarly, each wing must check the other’s power and maintain dedication to the cause, lest it devolve into a rehash of Trotsky’s “deformed workers’ state.” After all, I am my neighbors’ keeper- and they are mine. Rebuilding Anew Let’s say we’re successful: what sort of world might we win? The new order cannot replicate the traumas of the past one. Surely, there will be setbacks, hardships, and strife- such is the human condition. It is in how we address these ills and take steps to minimize harm that we find the true value of such a system. I have a three-point strategy for inculcating buy-in from the people, namely by addressing their material needs first and foremost. People have certain needs to live, and will require a decent standard of living to enjoy their newfound liberation. People oppressed may say such subjugation suffices if they are comfortable enough, allowing for a backslide

author: MTCSTW
text: ds to live, and will require a decent standard of living to enjoy their newfound liberation. People oppressed may say such subjugation suffices if they are comfortable enough, allowing for a backslide into capitalist exploitation unless material comfort is provided for the traumatized masses. Land Reform First and foremost, land should not be commodified and packaged and sold off to the highest bidder. A system of popular ownership should be imposed at first to strip landowning elites (Blackrock, absentee landlords, slumlords, and the like) of their shadily-gotten holdings. Each household would have use of a primary residence and no more. No leeching others dry by charging rents, no encampments of unhoused people, no deathtrap slums that endanger people who line the pockets of the owner class. Moving would be allowable through a housing swap program, though once people feel connected to one another in their communities I should hope emigration would be minimal. Jobs Guarantees Anyone who wants a job should be provided one, along with retraining and education at zero point-of-service cost, paid for via taxation and leverage of popularly-owned resources (nationalized natural resources, intellectual property, technologies, and products developed with public support, etc.). The jobs would be oriented toward public service, infrastructure building, civil administration, and other necessary functions. By ensuring that those who can work will be employed, material deprivation will b

title: After The Fall: Getting To The Future We Deserve
author: MTCSTW
text: would be oriented toward public service, infrastructure building, civil administration, and other necessary functions. By ensuring that those who can work will be employed, material deprivation will become a distant memory. Basic Needs Met By Default What if someone is disabled, or wants to pursue artistic endeavors, or otherwise wants to have a non-traditional means of contributing to society? This would be supported at the individual level by communal programs which provide universal basic housing, basic food, and basic medical care, as well as an allowance to use for incidentals and amenities up to a limit scaled based on the cost of living in the area in which they live and participate in communal governance. Should they want to supplement this amount, part-time or lighter-duty work would be assigned. A New Age Such a society would afford us greater freedom to pursue our dreams, enjoy our lives, and get to know our neighbors. We could finally be human to one another, and move in ways that inflict less harm on one another. This new age must come before the dissolution of the state, as – at its best – a state should seek only to secure rights for the citizenry and no more. Once popular control can be returned to the hands of the people, the state must be peeled away, like petals falling from a rose as it loses its relevance in fall, having seeded new life and fulfilled its central purpose. title: After The Fall: Getting To The Future We Deserve
author: MTCSTW
text: s falling from a rose as it loses its relevance in fall, having seeded new life and fulfilled its central purpose. How Do We Get There? In order to get to this world, we must first change the one we’re in into a transitory state of socialism before a fully communized society can be realized. Participation in popular movements, unions, co-ops, and other structures will provide an opportunity for uniting disparate peoples under a shared banner. Whichever wing you see fits you best should be explored and grown. Cross-wing dual-functionaries will be necessary as well, to coordinate between the two flanks. Think of them as the brain that signals to the heart how fast and to where blood must be pumped throughout the revolution, and which dictates which direction the arms must swing. Once the apparatus gains strength, material wins must be secured and built upon at an ever-accelerating pace, as momentum is essential for building the force necessary to overcome reactionary elements in society. With a series of key victories, including social, political, and cultural shifts toward egalitarian socialism, the stage is set. All it needs now are the players. title: Sick Left Radical Book Club Does "Pedagogy of the Oppressed," by Paolo Freire
author: MTCSTW
text: Something gentle happens when adults decide to learn together. We can stop performing. Not compare credentials. Finally stop reposting someone else’s analysis. — In community, we meet real curiosity. The kind where you read something triggering, sit with it, and then address another human and say: “Okay. But how can we do this in real life?” — Last month I met with a comrade from Vegas to try it out. We decided to start reading “Pedagogy of the Oppressed” by Paulo Freire. Join the Sick Left Radical Network! Subscribe Why This Book Freire wrote “Pedagogy of the Oppressed” to expose the quiet lie most of us were raised inside. That lie is: education is to be given knowledge. Teacher speaks. Students listen. Information is deposited like money in a bank. — Freire called this the banking model of education. In this model, students become containers. The teacher holds knowledge. The students receive it. Everyone plays their part. And the system stays exactly the same. Freire believed this kind of education doesn’t create thinkers… it creates compliance. Once you notice it, you start seeing the banking model everywhere: Corporate trainings. Professional development seminars. Media commentary. Political messaging. — A small number of people presenting themselves as the holders of truth, while everyone else absorbs. Freire proposed something much more radical; Human beings should learn through dialogue. Not in top-down instruction, but in conversation with each other. The 5 Questions

title: Sick Left Radical Book Club Does "Pedagogy of the Oppressed," by Paolo Freire
author: MTCSTW
text: while everyone else absorbs. Freire proposed something much more radical; Human beings should learn through dialogue. Not in top-down instruction, but in conversation with each other. The 5 Questions We Started With Instead of reading and then summarizing the entire book, we just started by asking a handful of questions. That real introspective shit. 1. What is Learning vs. Being Filled? Think about the last classroom or training you attended. Did you feel invited to think? Or did you feel like a container someone was filling with information? Freire argues that when people are treated like receptacles, they stop seeing themselves as thinkers. They adapt to the system instead of questioning it. Which is extremely convenient for the system. 2. What is Security vs. Freedom? Freire also writes about something uncomfortable: the fear of freedom. Freedom means living with uncertainty. Freedom means holding a greater responsibility. Freedom means having to constantly choose. That’s a lot harder than following instructions. So sometimes people choose the safety of a system they already know, even when that system harms or limits them. 3. What is Charity vs. Solidarity? Freire makes a sharp distinction between false generosity and true solidarity. False generosity offers help while leaving the unequal system intact. True solidarity asks a harder question: Why does this suffering exist in the first place? And what would it take to dismantle the structures producing it? — Helping peop

title: Sick Left Radical Book Club Does "Pedagogy of the Oppressed," by Paolo Freire
author: MTCSTW
text: ing the unequal system intact. True solidarity asks a harder question: Why does this suffering exist in the first place? And what would it take to dismantle the structures producing it? — Helping people matters. But treating people as equals matters more. 4. What is a Real Conversation? Freire describes dialogue as a horizontal relationship built on trust, humility, and curiosity. Not debate. Not lectures. Real encounters where both people are learning. Ask yourself honestly: How often do you experience that kind of conversation? 5. What is the Difference Between Thinking vs. Doing? Freire uses a word that appears across liberation movements: praxis. Praxis means reflection and action working together. Too much reflection without action leads to negative outcomes, including talking endlessly and forming committees while nothing changes. Too much action without reflection becomes empty activism—motion without strategy. Real community transformation requires both. The Sentence That Won’t Leave My Brain Freire drops a line that feels like a lightning strike for a white woman like me: “No one can be authentically human while he prevents others from being so.” Let’s pause and sit with that. … … … Oppression doesn’t just harm the oppressed. It distorts the humanity of everyone involved. Which means liberation isn’t just about winning power. It’s about transforming the conditions that make domination possible in the first place. The Goal: Conscientização Freire’s framework ultimatel

text: . Which means liberation isn’t just about winning power. It’s about transforming the conditions that make domination possible in the first place. The Goal: Conscientização Freire’s framework ultimately points toward something he calls conscientização. Critical, intersectional class consciousness. The ability to see the social, political, and economic contradictions shaping the world AND to act against them . In this process, people stop being objects of history. They become subjects who CAN shape it. If you want to join the conversation: Join the Propaganda Factory on Discord Join MTCSTW’s subscriber chat Available in the Substack app and on web Join chat 1. Read a small section of the book, whatever speaks to you We’re gonna be focused on “Pedagogy of the Oppressed” until enough comrades reach conscientização. 2. Stay for a short conversation We can meet once a week. Thirty minutes. 3. Bring your questions & impressions Confusion is welcome. Disagreement is welcome. Curiosity and respect is required. — That’s it. The goal is not to perform expertise. The goal is to practice thinking together. Why We’re Doing This Because the internet is full of opinions but is starved for understanding. Because people are drowning in information but rarely given the space and time to process it. And because if Freire is right, liberation doesn’t begin with a perfectly executed strategy. It begins when ordinary people learn how to think together again. author: MTCSTW
text: When people say who they are, listen to them “…nothing will fundamentally change…” -Joe Biden, to a room full of wealthy donors Boy, was he right about that. It's not the time for “peaceful” demonstrations- not as the only tool deployed by the “opposition party.” Friction makes heat, and we need to light a fire under the asses of the American people. It may be our last chance; I fear even if we act now, we'll be arriving a day late and a dollar short. Change has always come as a result of conflict that arises from irreconcilable tensions, not by asking very politely for the jackboots to be removed from our necks. Times like these call for an approach that employs a variety of tactics. I am not calling for armed revolution, or sabotage, or undermining rogue institutions from within- I'm not advocating for anything in particular, even, besides acting in stark defiance of this bloodthirsty regime. Do not act rashly and provide an excuse for a state of emergency and subsequent martial law announcements . I have seen neoliberalism demonstrate it's insufficiency over and over and over again during times of crisis. I’m old enough to remember enough social movements that got co-opted, Cointelpro'd, and cut down by those in power that it seems useless to keep trying. title: The Gentle General Reports for Duty
author: MTCSTW
text: I’m Sarah — creator of The Neurodivergent Report , contributor to The Propaganda Factory, and you’re now watching me step into my role here as the Gentle General. Yeah… that’s intentional juxtaposition built into my title. Because not all leaders need to shout to be assertive. Some of us are watching the play. Some of us are making stock. Some of us are bringing everyone water before we march. Who am I? I come to this coalition from the world of neurodiversity, psychology, chronic illness, and frazzled nervous systems. (SEE MORE : The Neurodivergent Report ) I study psychology, sociology, hierarchy, and power… I’m exposing the propaganda that people are taught to believe about being defective, all because they are refusing to be complicit in a dehumanizing social system. My other work is not separate from this one. It is the same cyclical pattern, just from a different intersectional awareness. How I’m Raging Against This Machine The Propaganda Factory is building networks, amplifying voices, and countering billionaire narratives at scale. My role? I help comrades understand what’s happening inside their own bodies while we do the work. Because here’s what I’m seeing over and over: Brilliant sick left radicals who are chronically dysregulated and out of commission. Organizers running on fumes. Comrades internalizing shame over lapses in executive functioning. Chronically ill folks wondering if there’s even a place for them in the movement. … There is. As the late great Fred R

title: The Gentle General Reports for Duty

title: Folks, It's High Time For Mass Mobilization
author: MTCSTW
text: I write primarily political commentary and analysis, though not dry policy wonk shit like a lot of others do. My work is driven and informed by my time as a street medic/black bloc protester, spanning 2019-2022. I draw on the lessons I learned in that era to inform my approach to political analysis: always consider multiple intersecting forces within even the simplest conflict, and class war is waged every day by the wealthy and the armed wings of the state theyve captured (most PDs, ICE/CBP, FBI, etc). Direct Action and Learning to Organize My work as an organizer began with the "Sanctuary City Now!" movement in Colorado Springs, and I stayed largely active throughout the pandemic/BLM Summer and afterward until I moved back east. I began writing SLSC as a way to help shift the Overton Window toward a future we deserve rather than the calamity we've been practically begging for. I use sharp/direct/idiosyncratic writing as a political tool specifically attempting to help mobilize the working poor. People deserve to have agency regarding how their own society functions, but in order to take it back we must act quickly and as one. If you're reading this, today could be the beginning of your political awakening. We will need every working person, lumpenprole, slacker, gutterpunk, ne'erdo'ell, and anyone else left behind by the capitalists and the Professional Managerial Class that serves them with glee for little more than extra crumbs. What better place than here, what better time than now? Be aware of what the work may entail You might get arrested, and there's a good chance you'll be hit with pepper balls, or exposed to tear gas, or get kettled by cops who herd protesters like cattle. If you're really making waves, you might get questioned, or arrested on trumped up charges meant to intimidate you into going back to quietly occupying the role they assigned to you: just a source of labor value to be exploited and then discarded when no longer productive. These are all hurdles that, alone, anyone would struggle with. When we band together, though, something changes in the equation. Support, solidarity, and compassion from everyone with whom you'll share a common cause is a source of strength you can tap into when things feel the most desperate. Human beings are social animals, and we function best when working collectively and collaboratively- not fragmented, isolated, and alienated from both ourselves and the world we live in- less a bug than a feature under late-stage capitalism; if we are all isolated and only function as individuals, capitalists and the petit-bourgoise will continue to dominate and dictate our conditions of living. We're In a “Zig or Zag” Moment There is no going back to brunch anymore. That ship left the harbor about a decade ago.

title: Who's Really Lazy Here?
author: MTCSTW
text: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than it is for a rich man to gain entrance to heaven. There is a deeply committed belief in this country that poor people are lazy. Not unlucky . Not underpaid. Not crushed by systems that were designed to extract from them until there’s nothing left. Lazy. That view is skewed in favor of the wealthy, and it is the wealthy who perpetuate this lie. Human beings used to know the difference between success and moral value, how the two were often linked in such a way that the more wealth you amassed, the harder it was to maintain any kind of moral well-being. The line above from the New Testament illustrates perfectly the proper way to look at those in society who exploit laborers, step on or over others on the way to the top, and who once there look for ways to wall off entrance by anyone else. title: Who's Really Lazy Here?
author: MTCSTW
text: suckers? In the 1980s, the “lazy poor” were caricatures - welfare queens, loafers, people who “just didn’t want to work.” Then everyone started working even harder . They would never call us lazy unless we were, right? So the working poor worked even more, over the next decades. A couple generations later what do we have? Multiple jobs. Side hustles. Gigs. Apps. Closing shifts lead into opening shifts, weekends folded into weekdays until time itself felt like an unpaid internship. God help you if your work is primarily domestic labor or care work, because that’s hard to profit off of, and therefore isn’t valued as “real work.” But in spite of all this degradation, the poor chug along, working harder and harder, watching the GDP rise year after year while wages stagnate. And yet the accusation didn’t go away. Now it’s: Why don’t you drive Uber on your days off? Why don’t you sell stuff online? Why don’t you learn to code? As if the problem is a lack of creativity, not a lack of money. Here’s the thing they never explain: if people are so lazy, why are they exhausted? You don’t get burnout from idleness. You get it from constantly running and never arriving anywhere that feels stable. You get it from doing everything you were told to do and still coming up short. From realizing that no amount of effort can outrun rents that jump faster than wages, groceries that cost more every month, or healthcare bills that show up like a mugger with paperwork. When your boss won’t give you enough hours, but the delivery app promises you “freedom.” When your full-time job still doesn’t pay rent, but there’s always another platform eager to skim a percentage off your survival. Yet, after all that, the scolding continues. If you’re struggling, it’s because you didn’t budget hard enough. Didn’t grind hard enough. Didn’t optimize yourself like a LinkedIn post with legs. Poverty is framed as a personal failure, because admitting it’s structural would require changing the structure - and that’s inconvenient for the people benefiting from it. So instead, we get lectures about “work ethic” from people whose wealth compounds while they sleep. People who call passive income a virtue and survival labor a character flaw. People who haven’t had to choose between gas and groceries in years, but still feel qualified to explain why you’re doing life wrong. The cruelty is the point. The instability and precarity are their stated goals. If you can convince people that struggling is a moral failing, you don’t have t

author: MTCSTW
text: to explain why you’re doing life wrong. The cruelty is the point. The instability and precarity are their stated goals. If you can convince people that struggling is a moral failing, you don’t have to fix anything. You don’t have to raise wages, regulate rents, or treat housing and healthcare like the necessities they are. You just have to keep everyone busy, tired, and blaming themselves. And it mostly works. The “lazy poor” don’t exist. What exists is a working class that’s been stretched thin, told it’s not enough, and then shamed for collapsing under the weight. The “lazy” ones in my mind are the rentier class slumlords, the hedge fund managers, the venture capital vultures- the real menaces to society who hurt via both action and inaction; how they amass their hoards hurts, but how they prevent anything from changing for the betterment of others hurts even more. People don’t need more motivation. They don’t need a TedX talk, or a self-help book, or any of that nonsense. Y’know what they do need though? Fewer traps. They need systems that don’t punish them for being alive and needing basics necessities of life. They need an economy that doesn’t require martyrdom just to scrape by. title: Kalshi Partners With CNN To Increase Rates Of Gambling Addiction
author: MTCSTW
text: If you like my writing, please also subscribe to my projects at SLSC On Substack , as well as The Neurodivergent News Network . The first is a class-first analysis of sciopolitical issues without sacrificing any group in the process, while 3N is focused more on those issues through the lens of neurodivergents in my network (guest writers are welcome!). In a move so gross it shocked even the most jaded observers of late-stage capitalism, CNN is partnering with Kalshi, a prediction-market app (read: betting parlor on your phone), to plaster live betting odds on the screen during coverage. Wolf Blitzer. AC 360. Elections, court rulings, foreign policy flare-ups, economic gut-punches - now with a scrolling price tag, like democracy just hit the discount rack. And now with sports, Fanduel! They’ll sell it as “context.” A tool for understanding uncertainty. The “wisdom of crowds.” The market as some kind of benevolent, all-knowing referee. That story collapses the second the ticker appears. Share Share The Propaganda Factory Because once odds are embedded in the news, you’re not just reporting events - you’re pricing them. The question stops being “what happened and who does it hurt?” and becomes “where’s the line moving?” Human stakes get blurred into background noise while the probability you can cash in on a tragedy takes center stage, glowing softly like it deserves your respect. And markets don’t measure truth. They measure incentives. And these incentives are so perverse they

And these incentives are so perverse they need a leash, a collar, and skin-tight, assless leather chaps. Prediction markets reward speed, confidence, and disposable cash. Not expertise. Not care. Not the ability to sit with a grieving parent or a terrified family and understand that “volatility” is just a bloodless way of saying people’s lives are getting flipped upside down . Not because viewers are stupid—but because humans absorb signals whether we want to or not. A candidate “trading” at 28¢ doesn’t feel like a long shot anymore. It feels like a waste of effort. A policy outcome that’s “priced in” starts to feel inevitable. Resistance quietly mutates into resignation, dressed up as realism. That’s the trick. It doesn’t have to silence you. It just has to convince you you’ve already lost. And then there’s the rot at the center of the whole thing. Sports betting is already a mess, but at least the athletes signed up to be in the arena. text: ng is already a mess, but at least the athletes signed up to be in the arena. Prediction markets turn everyone else into the arena. You’re betting on elections that decide whether people keep basic rights. On court rulings that determine who gets protected and who gets crushed. On wars, outbreaks, layoffs, a genocide in Gaza - outcomes that will land hardest on people who never consented to be converted into a line chart. The people placing the bets are usually the least likely to bleed from the result. The people who will bleed don’t get a cut of the upside. They just get to live inside whatever outcome the market decided was “probable.” Leave a comment So why would CNN do this? Because cable news is starving. Viewership is down. Trust is down. Ad money is jittery. And “interactive” keeps eyeballs glued to the screen. A live odds ticker feels like motion. It feels like participation. It gives viewers something to watch besides the slow realization that the country is being hollowed out in real time. It’s the same logic as sports gambling; skin in the game makes the game more fun. This game just happens to be guessing how much misery the world will experience. And once that infrastructure exists, it never stops with elections. Anything that can be quantified can be priced. Anything predicted can be priced and bet on. Anything bet on can be televised. Bully for them. At that point, the news isn’t a public service - it’s a casino floor with better fonts and a very serious voice
